chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Wilson's offer to Hinton and his loyalty to Al Hall
summary: Hinton recalls Wilson offering him a job in the new big band at lower pay but keeping the bassist he had started with, Al Hall.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But when you started that big band, you called me and offered me a job, and I don't know if you remember that, Teddy, but you're such a beautiful human being, and I got to tell you this, man, and it's got to go down as a matter of record and when you called and said, 'Milt, I'd like to have you join us, because I'd been making records with you and like you so much,' and the salary wasn't going to be the same salary that I was making with Cab -- but of course, I couldn't take a cut, and I said thank you -- and you said to
me, and I shall never forget these words, you said, 'Milt, I tell you this, I'd like to have you -- but whoever I start with I'm gonna keep' and you got Al Hall and you kept him.

And I can remember the respect I had for you, for being faithful -- and you've always done that. You didn't say if you got free later, I promise you the job -- and that has got to be highly respected.
Yeah, because we got to be like a close knit rhythm section, a family thing, everybody was friends.
